props.gloss_en: the first shearing applies in the Land and outside the Land
in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple
with non-sacred animals
but not with consecrated animals
there is a stringency in the foreleg, the jaw and the maw over the first shearing
for the foreleg, the jaw and the maw apply to cattle and to sheep
to many and to few
and the first shearing applies only to ewes
and applies only to many
how many is 'many'? Beit Shammai: two ewes
Beit Shammai's verse: 'a man shall rear a young cow and two sheep' (Isa 7:21)
Beit Hillel: five
Beit Hillel's verse: 'five sheep made ready' (I Sam 25:18)
R' Dosa ben Harkinas: five ewes shearing a maneh and a peras each are obligated in the first shearing
the Sages: five ewes shearing any amount at all
how much does one give him? the weight of five sela in Judea
which are ten sela in the Galilee
[that weight] laundered and not soiled
enough to make a small garment from it
as it is said 'you shall give him' (Deut 18:4) -- that there be in it enough for a gift
if he did not manage to give it to him until he dyed it -- exempt
if he laundered it and did not dye it -- obligated
one who buys the shearing of a gentile's flock is exempt from the first shearing
one who buys the shearing of his fellow's flock: if [the seller] kept some, the seller is obligated
if he kept none, the buyer is obligated
if he had two kinds, grey and white, and sold him the grey but not the white, the males but not the females -- this one gives for himself and that one gives for himself
